answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label reporting is the analytics and reporting work MMC does for your agency: tracking set-up, dashboards and monthly client reports built in your format and branding. It saves your team the hours spent pulling numbers, and gives your client a report that explains what happened and what to do next.

stages.breaks: Pulling numbers by hand every month.
stages.why: Your best strategist spends the last days of the month in spreadsheets instead of advising.
stages.does: Sources are connected once and refreshed on schedule, so the numbers are ready when the writing starts.

stages.why: A wrong conversion count is worse than none, because your client will act on it.
stages.does: We audit tags, events and attribution before the first report and note any known gaps in plain words.

stages.breaks: Building a new report layout for each client.
stages.why: Every client gets a different pack, nothing is reusable, and quality depends on who built it.
stages.does: Your template, with your branding and a fixed section order, is applied to every client.

stages.why: Clients cannot read a chart for what to do next, so they ask you, or they leave.
stages.does: Each report says what happened, what to watch and the one change we suggest, ready for your edit.

stages.why: Spend can look healthy while contribution margin shrinks, and no one is told.
stages.does: Where your client shares cost data, we add margin-aware views so decisions follow profit, not only platform figures.
